lines_of_business: Not stated by line of business; Benefit Application says determinations follow member health services contract language
effective_or_revised: Original 04/05/2007; Effective Aug 1, 2026 as printed (library metadata says 07/01/2023)
sections_in_order: Policy Guidelines (incl. Types of Devices, Coding)
Appendix A (before/after redline of policy statement)
criteria_location: Policy Statement pp.1-2 (I-IV). Policy Guidelines p.2 restate some of it. Pages ~7-50 are rationale/evidence; Codes pp.52-57; Appendix A pp.68-70 is a before/after redline that repeats the criteria in old and new wording.
procedures_covered: External AEM / continuous ambulatory monitors >48 h

logic.top_level: pathways (I external, II implantable, III MCOT, IV investigational list), each any-of
logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: Section IV lists investigational uses (MCOT for other conditions, asymptomatic monitoring with risk factors, antiarrhythmic effectiveness, ST-segment ischemia). MCOT prerequisite allows 'nondiagnostic or contraindicated' external monitor.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Holter monitor and/or external AEM has been nondiagnostic or contraindicated
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: 'and/or' plus 'nondiagnostic or contraindicated' creates four readings; no definition of either

and_or_ambiguity.quote: long-term monitoring with an external event monitor, OR a continuous ambulatory monitor ... OR an implantable ambulatory monitor may be considered medically necessary
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Policy Guidelines say the three device types are interchangeable for stroke/ablation indications, so a checker cannot enforce the I -> II -> III escalation implied elsewhere

requirement_kinds.quote: Infrequent symptoms (less frequently than every 48 hours) suggestive of cardiac arrhythmias (i.e., palpitations, dizziness, presyncope, or syncope)
To guide discontinuation of systemic anticoagulation in individuals with history of atrial fibrillation (AF) and prior catheter ablation
History of cryptogenic stroke with a negative standard workup for AF including a 24-hour Holter monitor
Recurrent symptoms ... and a negative prior evaluation with external ambulatory event monitors
Symptoms are thought to be due to a cardiac arrhythmia as the most likely diagnosis
Holter monitor and/or external AEM has been nondiagnostic or contraindicated
There is documentation that real-time monitoring is essential for patient safety and will lead to immediate clinical changes such as medication or other emergent procedures
Evaluation of cryptogenic stroke thought to be caused by atrial fibrillation, with non-diagnostic 24- to 48-hour Holter monitor or 48-hour telemetry

thresholds.quote: record and store information for periods longer than 48 hours
non-diagnostic 24- to 48-hour Holter monitor or 48-hour telemetry

codes.codes_tied_to_criteria: Codes in a table by type, not mapped to criteria; stated as 'general reference'
codes.non_covered_code_lists: Code table includes 0497T/0498T etc.; no separate non-covered list found

external_dependencies.what: Contract language controls; state/federal law may require FDA-approved services
2025 specialty-society clinical input (HRS, ACC EP Council) used to justify MCOT criteria
external_dependencies.quote: clinical input was received from 3 respondents

vague_terms.problem: MCOT uses 'clinically significant' and 'severe palpitations' but external AEM uses plain palpitations; no grading
standard workup beyond Holter not defined

vague_terms.quote: essential for patient safety and will lead to immediate clinical changes
vague_terms.problem: prediction about future care; rarely in a chart

extraction_hazards: 70 pages, about 55 are evidence review and references; criteria are only the first 2 pages
Appendix A is a redline with before/after columns and red/blue font; pdftotext interleaves old and new text, so old criteria (e.g., MCOT = investigational) look current
Appendix 1 repeats MCOT criteria as clinical input
Effective date printed Aug 1 2026 vs library note 07/01/2023
interesting_structures: Policy Guidelines make device types interchangeable for stroke and post-ablation
MCOT justified by 2025 society input; Appendix A shows MCOT moved from investigational to conditionally necessary
Real-time monitoring must be 'essential for patient safety' (unusual)

fit_to_tree.why: Clear any/all blocks, but criteria are scattered across Policy Statement, Policy Guidelines, Additional Information and Appendix A in several versions, and several leaves are predictions or undefined.
